In 2024, one of India's biggest wallets was frozen.
Now, it's getting a second life.
Then came demonetisation, and Paytm was everywhere.
In 2017, the wallet moved into Paytm's own bank.
And banks face much stricter rules.
2022. The RBI stopped it from adding new customers.
January 2024. No more deposits, no wallet top-ups.
And this April, the RBI cancelled the bank's licence.
So how is the wallet coming back?
Through a different Paytm company, Paytm Payments Services.
On November thirteenth, the RBI gave it an in-principle nod to run wallets.
Think of it as a learner's licence.
Paytm must clear a cyber-security audit within six months, or the approval lapses.
Same app. New company behind the wallet.
Would you load money into Paytm again?
